description: Two-arm matmul microbenchmark that can discriminate bandwidth from MXU tiling, replacing M15 which could not. Every cell reports implied GB/s and FLOP/s; cells below a utilisation floor are refused rather than interpreted.
note_floor: M15 ran at 7% of peak bandwidth and its curve was per-dispatch overhead. Any cell below 20% of either roof is dispatch-bound and is reported but not interpreted.

arms.name: real_shapes
arms.note: Real qkv shape, amortised over 200 iterations so dispatch is divided away. Tests m13's frontier: flat to M~240, rising after.

arms.name: tile_probe
arms.note: 2048x2048 = 8.4 MB, small enough to plausibly stay VMEM-resident across the 1000 loop iterations. That is the ONLY way to get compute-bound below M=241: for a weight-stationary matmul the arithmetic intensity IS M, so a per-iteration HBM reload makes every M<241 bandwidth-bound no matter how the matrix is sized. If the weights are not hoisted, this arm stays under the utilisation floor and is refused rather than misread -- which is the correct outcome, not a failure.

note_intensity: Recorded because it invalidated the first design of this experiment: a weight-stationary matmul with M rows has arithmetic intensity exactly M, so no choice of matrix size makes M<241 compute-bound on this chip. Only amortising the weight load across iterations can.
